newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ indexed bonds good value at 5.8-5.9 pct - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ indexed bonds good value at 5.8-5.9 pct - BTNZ.

text.p: The inflation-indexed bonds on offer by the New Zealand Debt Management Office on Thursday represent value between 5.8 percent and 5.9 percent, Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Wednesday.
The DMO will offer NZ$50 million of February 2016 inflation-indexed bonds.
BTNZ said yields could be pushed towards the lower end of their 5.8-5.9 percent range by investors seeking some pre-election insurance against a "bond negative" outcome.
"Political polls show that a centre-left government remains a very real possibility after the October 12 election.

"Such an outcome would almost certainly see a tolerance of higher inflation, and greater government spending, both of which would be worse for conventional bonds in comparison with inflation indexed bonds," BTNZ said.
It said real yields just under six percent on inflation indexed bonds continued to offer very good real returns to investors.
Yields have drifted down slightly since the last inflation-indexed bond tender on July 25, with NZ 10-year conventional bond yields falling to 8.17 percent from 8.38 percent.
BTNZ said the spread between NZ and US 10-year conventional bonds had narrowed to 137 basis points from 152 on July 25.

Over a slightly longer period, the NZ/US 10-year conventional bond spread had fallen from a peak of over 200 basis points in June. In the same period, the spread between NZ inflation-indexed and conventional bonds had falled to 230 basis points from a peak of over 300 basis points.

BTNZ said since the last tender, indexed bond pricing had been affected by a number of factors. These included political opinion polls showing a very real possibility of a centre-left government after the election.

In addition, surveys had suggested a slight increase in inflation expectations, and the Reserve Bank had reiterated in its September economic forecasts that there was no scope for an easing in monetary conditions until it saw conclusive evidence that inflation pressures were abating.
